<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
- end your program with `#show output/3.`
</rules>

<example_1>
This puzzle copies the input to the output unchanged.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Recolor every non-zero cell to 5; zeros stay 0.
output(R, C, 5) :- input(R, C, V), V != 0.
output(R, C, 0) :- input(R, C, 0).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_2>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color

% Mirror: column C of the output is column (M-1-C) of the input.
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, Cin, Color), n_cols(M), C = M - 1 - Cin.

#show output/3.
</asp>

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.

% Row and column indices
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output cell must exist for every cell
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Determine orientation:
% orient_rows is true if the grid has more rows than columns
orient_rows :- R > C.
orient_cols :- C > R.

% Exactly one of the two orientations holds
1 { orient_rows : R > C } 1 { orient_cols : C > R }.

% Determine the integer k = floor(larger / smaller)
% larger = max(R,C) and smaller = min(R,C)
% For rows orientation: larger = R, smaller = C
k(K) :- orient_rows, K*C <= R, (K+1)*C > R.
% For columns orientation: larger = C, smaller = R
k(K) :- orient_cols, K*R <= C, (K+1)*R > C.

% Period = 2 * k  (period is always even)
period(P) :- k(K), P = 2*K.

% List each non‑zero cell
colored(R0,C0,Color) :- input(R0,C0,Color).

%--- Orientation: rows -------------------------------------------------
% Map a residue S to a colour for row orientation
% There is a colour for every residue that is the residue of a coloured cell
stripe_color_rows(S, Color) :- colored(R0,C0,Color), orient_rows,
                         period(P), S, Q, R0 = P*Q + S.

% Fill all rows that have this residue with that colour
output(R,C,Color) :- stripe_color_rows(S,Color), row(R), col(C),
                     1 { Q : R = P*Q + S }.

%--- Orientation: columns ----------------------------------------------
% Map a residue S to a colour for column orientation
stripe_color_cols(S, Color) :- colored(R0,C0,Color), orient_cols,
                         period(P), S, Q, C0 = P*Q + S.

% Fill all columns that have this residue with that colour
output(R,C,Color) :- stripe_color_cols(S,Color), row(R), col(C),
                     1 { Q : C = P*Q + S }.

% Exactly one colour per output cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.

% Row and column indices
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output cell must exist for every cell
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Determine orientation:
% orient_rows is true if the grid has more rows than columns
orient_rows :- R > C.
orient_cols :- C > R.

% Exactly one of the two orientations holds
1 { orient_rows : R > C } 1 { orient_cols : C > R }.

% Determine the integer k = floor(larger / smaller)
% larger = max(R,C) and smaller = min(R,C)
% For rows orientation: larger = R, smaller = C
k(K) :- orient_rows, K*C <= R, (K+1)*C > R.
% For columns orientation: larger = C, smaller = R
k(K) :- orient_cols, K*R <= C, (K+1)*R > C.

% Period = 2 * k  (period is always even)
period(P) :- k(K), P = 2*K.

% List each non‑zero cell
colored(R0,C0,Color) :- input(R0,C0,Color).

%--- Orientation: rows -------------------------------------------------
% Map a residue S to a colour for row orientation
% There is a colour for every residue that is the residue of a coloured cell
stripe_color_rows(S, Color) :- colored(R0,C0,Color), orient_rows,
                         period(P), S, Q, R0 = P*Q + S.

% Fill all rows that have this residue with that colour
output(R,C,Color) :- stripe_color_rows(S,Color), row(R), col(C),
                     1 { Q : R = P*Q + S }.

%--- Orientation: columns ----------------------------------------------
% Map a residue S to a colour for column orientation
stripe_color_cols(S, Color) :- colored(R0,C0,Color), orient_cols,
                         period(P), S, Q, C0 = P*Q + S.

% Fill all columns that have this residue with that colour
output(R,C,Color) :- stripe_color_cols(S,Color), row(R), col(C),
                     1 { Q : C = P*Q + S }.

% Exactly one colour per output cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

#show output/3.
</asp>

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.

% Row and column indices
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output cell must exist for every cell
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Determine orientation:
% orient_rows is true if the grid has more rows than columns
orient_rows :- R > C.
orient_cols :- C > R.

% Exactly one of the two orientations holds
1 { orient_rows : R > C } 1 { orient_cols : C > R }.

% Determine the integer k = floor(larger / smaller)
% larger = max(R,C) and smaller = min(R,C)
% For rows orientation: larger = R, smaller = C
k(K) :- orient_rows, K*C <= R, (K+1)*C > R.
% For columns orientation: larger = C, smaller = R
k(K) :- orient_cols, K*R <= C, (K+1)*R > C.

% Period = 2 * k  (period is always even)
period(P) :- k(K), P = 2*K.

% Dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.

% Row and column indices
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Determine orientation (choose horizontal stripes when columns are not fewer than rows, otherwise vertical stripes)
col_orientation :- M >= N.   % includes equality
row_orientation :- N > M.

% Period: period = 2 * floor(larger / smaller)
% Horizontal orientation (columns are larger)
k_col(K) :- col_orientation, K * N <= M, (K+1) * N > M.
% Vertical orientation (rows are larger)
k_row(K) :- row_orientation, K * M <= N, (K+1) * M > N.

period(P) :- k_col(K), P = 2*K.
period(P) :- k_row(K), P = 2*K.

% List each colored cell
colored(R0,C0,Color) :- input(R0,C0,Color).

% Residues for stripes (when no conflict)
row_residue(S,Color) :- colored(R0,C0,Color), row_orientation, period(P), S, Q, R0 = P*Q + S, S < P.
col_residue(S,Color) :- colored(R0,C0,Color), col_orientation, period(P), S, Q, C0 = P*Q + S, S < P.

% Conflict detection: a conflict exists if some residue receives two different colors
conflict_row :- row_residue(S,Color1), row_residue(S,Color2), Color1 != Color2.
conflict_col :- col_residue(S,Color1), col_residue(S,Color2), Color1 != Color2.
conflict :- conflict_row; conflict_col.

% Choose rule: stripes when no conflict, mirror when conflict
% Stripes (horizontal when col_orientation, vertical when row_orientation)
output(R,C,Color) :- not conflict, col_orientation, col_residue(S,Color), row(R), col(C), 1 { Q : C = P*Q + S }.
output(R,C,Color) :- not conflict, row_orientation, row_residue(S,Color), row(R), col(C), 1 { Q : R = P*Q + S }.

% Mirror (horizontal when col_orientation, vertical when row_orientation)
output(R,C,Color) :- conflict, col_orientation, Cin = M-1 - C, input(R, Cin, Color), C = Cin.
output(R,C,Color) :- conflict, row_orientation, Rin = N-1 - R, input(Rin, C, Color), R = Rin.

% Exactly one color per output cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% Determine orientation:
% orient_rows is true if the grid has more rows than columns
orient_rows :- R > C.
orient_cols :- C > R.

% Exactly one of the two orientations holds
1 { orient_rows : R > C } 1 { orient_cols : C > R }.

% Determine the integer k = floor(larger / smaller)
% larger = max(R,C) and smaller = min(R,C)
% For rows orientation: larger = R, smaller = C

period(P) :- k(K), P = 2*K.

% ------------------------------------------------------------

col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Orientation – choose stripes when columns are not fewer than rows
%  (if equal we also use stripes – horizontal stripes)
% ------------------------------------------------------------
col_orientation :- M >= N.          % horizontal stripes (or equal)
row_orientation :- N > M.           % vertical stripes

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Period = 2 * floor(larger / smaller)
%  Horizontal orientation  (M is larger)
%  Vertical   orientation  (N is larger)
% ------------------------------------------------------------
k_col(K)  :- col_orientation, K * N <= M, (K+1) * N > M.
k_row(K)  :- row_orientation, K * M <= N, (K+1) * M > N.

period(P) :- k_col(K), P = 2*K.
period(P) :- k_row(K), P = 2*K.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  List every colored cell in the input
% ------------------------------------------------------------
colored(R0,C0,Color) :- input(R0,C0,Color).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Residues for the stripe rules (used only when there is no conflict)
% ------------------------------------------------------------
col_residue(S,Color) :- colored(R0,C0,Color), col_orientation,
                      period(P), S, Q, C0 = P*Q + S, S < P.

row_residue(S,Color) :- colored(R0,C0,Color), row_orientation,
                      period(P), S, Q, R0 = P*Q + S, S < P.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Detect a conflict: a residue receives two different colours
% ------------------------------------------------------------
conflict_row :- row_residue(S,Color1), row_residue(S,Color2), Color1 != Color2.
conflict_col :- col_residue(S,Color1), col_residue(S,Color2), Color1 != Color2.
conflict     :- conflict_row.       % true if any conflict exists
conflict     :- conflict_col.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
output(R,C,Color) :- not conflict,
                     col_orientation, col_residue(S,Color),
                     row(R), col(C), 1 { Q : C = P*Q + S }.

output(R,C,Color) :- not conflict,
                     row_orientation, row_residue(S,Color),
                     row(R), col(C), 1 { Q : R = P*Q + S }.

% ------------------------------------------------------------

                     col_orientation, Cin = M-1 - C,

                     row_orientation, Rin = N-1 - R,
                     input(Rin, C, Color).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
